Kinetic ABS Parent LLC and the Kinetic ABS obligors are unrestricted subsidiaries under the credit agreements and indentures (page:50). The Q2 10-Q gives a restricted versus unrestricted consolidating view of the balance sheet and statement of operations (page:50-51); the 10-K and earlier 10-Qs give the same view for their dates (10-K page:193-195; Q1 10-Q page:49; Q3 2025 10-Q page:66-67).

The senior secured credit facilities are guaranteed by Uniti Group Inc. and Uniti Group LLC on a senior unsecured basis and by certain wholly owned subsidiaries of Uniti Services on a senior secured basis (page:25). Asset-backed notes are issued by bankruptcy-remote subsidiaries: Uniti Fiber ABS Issuer LLC and Uniti Fiber TRS Issuer LLC for the Fiber Infrastructure ABS Notes, and Kinetic ABS Issuer LLC for the Kinetic ABS Notes (page:22, page:50). Kinetic ABS Parent LLC and the Kinetic ABS obligors are unrestricted subsidiaries under the credit agreements and indentures (page:50). The Q2 10-Q gives a restricted versus unrestricted consolidating view of the balance sheet and statement of operations (page:50-51); the 10-K and earlier 10-Qs give the same view for their dates (10-K page:193-195; Q1 10-Q page:49; Q3 2025 10-Q page:66-67).

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable with limitations. Reported figures for Q1 2026, Q2 2026 and the first half of 2026 come from filed statements on the combined-company perimeter and tie to the releases. FY2025 holds the combined company only from 2025-08-01, so trailing and annual metrics are not like-for-like and are labelled that way. On the filed numbers, total debt principal of 10,680.6 million stood at 7.16x trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 1,492.2 million, and 6.75x after deducting 608.9 million of unrestricted cash. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA covered trailing cash interest paid of 768.6 million 1.94 times. Interest expense, net was 383.9 million in the first half of 2026 against GAAP operating income of 143.1 million, so the company reports a net loss of 226.2 million for the half. Operating cash flow of 339.4 million fell short of capital expenditures of 799.2 million, and the gap was funded by debt: 2,072.6 million of issuance against 930.0 million of repayments. Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was cash of 608.9 million plus 838.1 million of revolver availability. Four limits bind every metric: Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure defined to resemble debt agreement terms but not tested here; the trailing period includes July 2025 without Windstream; covenant levels are not printed; and quarter-end debt does not include the July 2026 asset-backed issue or the planned repayments.

facts.label: Perimeter and period basis
facts.text: - Reporting entity: Uniti Group Inc. and subsidiaries, consolidated. Old Uniti is the accounting acquirer, so periods before 2025-08-01 show Old Uniti only and later periods show the combined company (Q2 10-Q page:11, page:19). - FY2025: audited, with PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP's opinion (10-K page:95-99). It contains seven months of Old Uniti and five months of the combined company. - 2026 quarters: unaudited, combined company. Their comparatives are Old Uniti only and recast for the reclassifications described in the Q2 10-Q (page:11-12). Year-on-year changes are therefore not organic. The Q2 10-Q states that Windstream contributed 795.9 million of the quarter's 909.7 million revenue (page:63). - FY2025 net income of 1,304.7 million includes a gain on settlement of preexisting relationships of 1,683.9 million (10-K page:101, page:88). The gain is excluded from Adjusted EBITDA. FY2025 reported EBITDA of 2,620.6 million (page:88) includes it and must not be used as a leverage denominator. - Fiber Infrastructure revenue fell from 300.7 million in Q2 2025 to 200.3 million of external revenue in Q2 2026 because Windstream lease revenue ended on the merger; the filing attributes the decrease to the settlement of the preexisting leasing relationships (Q2 10-Q page:47, page:70).

- FY2025: audited, with PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP's opinion (10-K page:95-99). It contains seven months of Old Uniti and five months of the combined company.

- 2026 quarters: unaudited, combined company. Their comparatives are Old Uniti only and recast for the reclassifications described in the Q2 10-Q (page:11-12). Year-on-year changes are therefore not organic. The Q2 10-Q states that Windstream contributed 795.9 million of the quarter's 909.7 million revenue (page:63).

- FY2025 net income of 1,304.7 million includes a gain on settlement of preexisting relationships of 1,683.9 million (10-K page:101, page:88). The gain is excluded from Adjusted EBITDA. FY2025 reported EBITDA of 2,620.6 million (page:88) includes it and must not be used as a leverage denominator.

- Fiber Infrastructure revenue fell from 300.7 million in Q2 2025 to 200.3 million of external revenue in Q2 2026 because Windstream lease revenue ended on the merger; the filing attributes the decrease to the settlement of the preexisting leasing relationships (Q2 10-Q page:47, page:70).

facts.label: Income statement and operating drivers
facts.text: - Revenue: Q2 2026 revenue was 909.7 million and Q1 2026 987.5 million. The Q1 figure includes the IRU sales revenue of 85.5 million for the first half; Q1 sales revenues were 98.5 million and Q2 56.8 million (Q1 10-Q page:4; Q2 10-Q page:4, page:63). Service revenues were 889.0 million in Q1 and 852.9 million in Q2, which is lower in Q2. - Margins: Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 357.1 million was below Q1 2026 at 441.6 million, and the 2026 outlook issued 2026-07-30 is Adjusted EBITDA of 1,450 to 1,500 million, interest expense, net of 805 million and a net loss of 480 to 530 million (release page:2). That outlook is a management forward-looking statement. First-half Adjusted EBITDA of 798.7 million implies a second-half range of 651.3 to 701.3 million to reach it (calculated). - Segments, Q2 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:47-49): Kinetic external revenue 528.2 and contribution margin 228.4; Fiber Infrastructure external revenue 200.3 and contribution margin 121.8; Uniti Solutions external revenue 181.2 and contribution margin 91.8; total segment contribution margin 442.0. facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Uniti Group Inc. is a Delaware holding company that survived the 2025-08-01 merger of Windstream and Old Uniti as the ultimate parent. Old Uniti was a REIT that owned and leased communications infrastructure, with Windstream as its anchor tenant; after the merger it ceased to be a REIT and the company does not qualify as one. The combined business has three segments. Kinetic sells consumer and small business broadband and voice in incumbent markets. Fiber Infrastructure sells enterprise, carrier and wholesale connectivity, including to hyperscalers, and holds the legacy fiber and leasing assets. Uniti Solutions sells managed network, security and collaboration services to enterprises. The credit story is the build-out of fiber to the home at Kinetic and of wholesale fiber, funded by debt. The creditor-relevant mechanics are these. First, the perimeter changed, so history before the merger is Old Uniti. Second, all pre-merger debt of Old Uniti and Windstream was merged into one borrower, Uniti Services LLC, with cross-guarantees and the removal of restrictive covenants that kept the groups apart. Third, since 2026-01-30 the company has financed Kinetic through asset-backed notes issued by bankruptcy-remote unrestricted subsidiaries that hold the fiber assets and customer contracts, which places those assets and their cash flows ahead of other creditors for those noteholders. Fourth, Elliott and its affiliates hold about 25.2% of the common stock and have rights tied to the preferred stock. Fifth, the company states that it does not intend to pay common dividends. No sponsor is named in the context. Behaviour toward creditors is read as neutral or mixed on documented actions: refinancing that extended the maturity profile and transparent disclosure of unrestricted subsidiary results on one side, and transfers of assets from guarantor subsidiaries into unrestricted asset-backed structures on the other. Legal capacity for those transfers depends on indenture terms that are not supplied.

Second, all pre-merger debt of Old Uniti and Windstream was merged into one borrower, Uniti Services LLC, with cross-guarantees and the removal of restrictive covenants that kept the groups apart. Third, since 2026-01-30 the company has financed Kinetic through asset-backed notes issued by bankruptcy-remote unrestricted subsidiaries that hold the fiber assets and customer contracts, which places those assets and their cash flows ahead of other creditors for those noteholders. Fourth, Elliott and its affiliates hold about 25.2% of the common stock and have rights tied to the preferred stock. Fifth, the company states that it does not intend to pay common dividends. No sponsor is named in the context. Behaviour toward creditors is read as neutral or mixed on documented actions: refinancing that extended the maturity profile and transparent disclosure of unrestricted subsidiary results on one side, and transfers of assets from guarantor subsidiaries into unrestricted asset-backed structures on the other. Legal capacity for those transfers depends on indenture terms that are not supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The Merger. On 2025-08-01 Windstream merged into the company, which survived as ultimate parent, and a merger subsidiary merged into Old Uniti, which survived as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary (Q2 10-Q page:9). Each Old Uniti share converted into 0.6029 shares of the company's common stock. Windstream's equityholders received about 90.1 million common shares, about 0.6 million preferred shares with a liquidation preference of 575.0, about 17.6 million warrants at a 0.01 dollar exercise price and 370.7 of cash, funded from Old Uniti's cash and revolver borrowings (page:10). The accounting is a reverse merger: Windstream was legal acquirer and Old Uniti was accounting acquirer (page:10). Total merger consideration was 2,376.6, made up of common stock 733.7, preferred stock 630.4, warrants 142.7, cash 370.7 and 499.1 attributed to the settlement of preexisting relationships (page:16). Those relationships were the Windstream Leases (an ILEC master lease and a CLEC master lease under which Old Uniti was Windstream's landlord), an asset purchase agreement and other leasing and supplier arrangements; they became intercompany and eliminated, and the leases were judged above market by 559.0 against an unfavourable asset purchase agreement of 60.0 (page:17-18). Status: complete; purchase price allocation finalised in Q2 2026 (page:18). Credit meaning: the Windstream lease payments that Old Uniti received as landlord ceased to be external revenue; creditors of the two former groups now rank in one structure.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Debt reorganisation. On 2025-08-04 Uniti Group LP, the borrower under Old Uniti's debt, was merged into Uniti Services LLC, formerly Windstream Services, LLC, the borrower under Windstream's debt. All debt became obligations of the same borrower, each subsidiary that guaranteed one group's debt guaranteed the other's, the Windstream revolver became pari passu with other first lien debt, and restrictive covenants that kept the groups apart were effectively eliminated (10-K page:56). Credit meaning: structural separation between the two creditor groups ended; the combined guarantor group supports all debt.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Uniti Group Inc. carries a weak fundamental credit profile with adequate near-term liquidity. The assessment is an Analyst Interpretation with Medium confidence. Financial risk dominates. At 2026-06-30 total debt principal of 10,680.6 million was 7.16x trailing Adjusted EBITDA and 6.75x net of unrestricted cash, and trailing Adjusted EBITDA covered trailing cash interest paid 1.94 times. Adjusted EBITDA is a company measure that excludes transaction costs and stock-based compensation, and the trailing window includes one pre-merger month. Cash generation does not support the investment programme: first-half 2026 operating cash flow of 339.4 million compared with capital expenditures of 799.2 million, so the build is financed with new debt, and the company reports a net loss in each of Q1 2026 and Q2 2026. Business risk is moderate. Uniti has three segments, no customer above 10% of revenue, a large fiber footprint, and a Kinetic fiber build that management intends to raise penetration and revenue per customer (management strategy), but the Fiber Infrastructure revenue base reset when Windstream's lease income ended on 2025-08-01, hyperscaler IRU revenue is lumpy, and the DSL base is declining. Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months: 1,447.0 million of cash and revolver availability at 2026-06-30, no instrument maturing before the 2027-12-01 convertible notes and the 2027-12-30 revolver maturities, and 1,140.7 million of further asset-backed proceeds in July 2026 of which 500.0 million is planned for secured debt repayment. Creditor control and structure add risk: the share of debt in non-recourse asset-backed subsidiaries is rising, and covenant levels and executed documents are not supplied. The credit view is therefore that earnings must grow into the debt through the fiber build while market access stays open; the filings contain no evidence that either is secured.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Leverage and cover are weak, and the apparent improvement is partly a perimeter effect. Total debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 8.13x at FY2025, 7.75x at the trailing period to Q1 2026 and 7.16x at the trailing period to Q2 2026, but each earlier ratio uses a window with fewer Windstream months, so the improvement is partly a perimeter effect rather than a deleveraging. Cash interest cover was 1.78x, 2.34x and 1.94x on the same windows. Mechanism (Analyst Interpretation): higher-cost debt added in 2026 (8.625% unsecured notes and the asset-backed notes) is likely to raise cash interest faster than Adjusted EBITDA at the current build stage. Implication: leverage tolerance is low and a modest earnings shortfall would push trailing cash interest cover to about 1.55x (illustrative, calculated below). - Free cash flow is structurally negative while the build runs. Operating cash flow less capital expenditures was negative 459.8 million in H1 2026 and negative 437.6 million in FY2025. Adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditures for the trailing period was 151.4 million (calculated below), which does not cover trailing cash interest paid of 768.6 million. Mechanism: capital expenditures at Kinetic of 602.8 million in H1 2026 front-load cost before subscriber revenue. citations.quote: Strengths:

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: - Scale and diversification of revenue. Three segments, no customer above 10% of revenue, and a network of about 240,000 fiber route miles (Documentary Fact, from the business handoff). Mechanism: reduces dependence on any one customer after the merger ended the dependence of Old Uniti on Windstream. Implication: lower single-customer default risk than before the merger. - Adequate near-term liquidity and no scheduled maturity before December 2027. Cash and revolver availability of 1,447.0 million, and no instrument maturing in the next twelve months other than term loan amortization (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Implication: low near-term refinancing and liquidity risk. - Demonstrated capital markets access. The company completed asset-backed notes in January and July 2026, 1.0 billion of unsecured notes in February 2026, and a secured refinancing in October 2025 that redeemed the 10.50% notes due 2028 (Documentary Fact). Implication: supports refinancing, though at high coupons. - Segment margins. Contribution margins of about 52% at Fiber Infrastructure, 50% at Uniti Solutions and 42% at Kinetic in Q2 2026 are stated by management (Management Language), before corporate costs. Implication: scope for operating leverage if revenue grows, not yet visible in cash flow. - No common dividends. The company states no intention to pay common dividends (Documentary Fact). Implication: cash is retained for the build and debt service. - Fiber customer growth. Kinetic fiber consumer broadband customers were 602.8 thousand at 2026-06-30 and management states record quarterly fiber net adds (Documentary Fact for the customer count; Management Language for the record claim). Implication: supports future recurring revenue, if build costs per premise are controlled, which is not shown.

citations.quote: Weaknesses:

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: - High leverage and thin cover. Total debt 7.16x and net debt 6.75x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, cash interest cover 1.94x (Documentary Fact and calculation from the financial base). Implication: little tolerance for earnings shortfalls or rate increases on the floating-rate term loan. - Negative free cash flow from the build. Operating cash flow of 339.4 million against capital expenditures of 799.2 million in H1 2026 (Documentary Fact). Implication: reliance on external funding. - GAAP losses. Net loss of 226.2 million in H1 2026 with interest expense, net of 383.9 million exceeding operating income of 143.1 million (Documentary Fact). Implication: earnings do not yet cover the interest burden on a GAAP basis. - Comparability and earnings quality. The perimeter changed on 2025-08-01, Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure, and Q1 2026 included IRU sales revenue of 85.5 million for the half that is not recurring service revenue (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on recurrence). Implication: run-rate earnings are harder to judge than reported trailing figures suggest. - Back-end loaded maturity wall and the shifting structure. Heavy 2031 to 2033 maturities, rising asset-backed debt in unrestricted subsidiaries, and a preferred stock claim with an Elliott repurchase right (Documentary Fact). Implication: refinancing risk is deferred rather than removed, and unsecured holders are more exposed to asset transfers. - Disclosure gaps and inconsistencies. No covenant levels, no executed documents, and two logged conflicts on ranking and the maturity table (Insufficient Information and Documentary Fact). Implication: the view cannot be tested against creditor protections.

### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested work with limitations. All four requested consumers are assessed as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, none CONDITIONAL and none BLOCKED. The pack holds one audited annual report, three unaudited quarterly reports and three earnings releases, all in USD, all dated on or before 2026-07-30 and so inside the cutoff. The binding limitations are four. First, the merger of 2025-08-01 changes the perimeter, so Old Uniti history before that date and combined history after it must not be set side by side as like for like. Second, no executed credit agreement, indenture, ABS indenture or supplement is supplied, so covenant levels, guarantor lists and security terms rest on filing summaries. Third, nothing after the filing of the second-quarter report on 2026-07-30 is supplied, including any third-quarter 2026 report. Fourth, the text extraction has not been reviewed for fidelity and no chart or image content exists to inspect. None of these blocks a consumer from starting, and each is carried forward as a stated limit.
### Source-by-source assessment

All seven sources identify Uniti Group Inc. as the registrant or the announcing company (page:1 of each). No source is blocked, draft, unsigned or a duplicate of another. The filed 10-K and 10-Qs control their own facts. The three releases are management claims and must not override the filings. The pack has no investor presentations; the retrieval record in the pack folder lists releases in their place, so no slide coverage is claimed or needed.

### Entity and perimeter

The registrant is Uniti Group Inc., the ultimate parent after the merger. On 2025-08-01 Windstream merged into the registrant and a merger subsidiary merged into Old Uniti, which survived as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary and ceased to be a REIT (Q2 10-Q page:9). The merger was accounted for as a reverse merger with Windstream as legal acquirer and Old Uniti as accounting acquirer, so periods before the merger show Old Uniti only (page:10-11). The Q2 10-Q states that Windstream is included from 2025-08-01 (page:19). The auditor of record changed: the FY2025 opinion is signed by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, "auditor since 2025" (10-K page:99), and a second report covers FY2024 and the year before it (10-K page:100).

Debt sits at several levels. Uniti Services LLC, CSL Capital, LLC and Uniti Group Finance 2019 Inc. are the borrowers under the Uniti Credit Agreement (page:23). Uniti Services, formerly Windstream Services, LLC, is the borrower under the Windstream Credit Agreement (page:24). The senior secured credit facilities are guaranteed by Uniti Group Inc. and Uniti Group LLC on a senior unsecured basis and by certain wholly owned subsidiaries of Uniti Services on a senior secured basis (page:25). Asset-backed notes are issued by bankruptcy-remote subsidiaries: Uniti Fiber ABS Issuer LLC and Uniti Fiber TRS Issuer LLC for the Fiber Infrastructure ABS Notes, and Kinetic ABS Issuer LLC for the Kinetic ABS Notes (page:22, page:50). Kinetic ABS Parent LLC and the Kinetic ABS obligors are unrestricted subsidiaries under the credit agreements and indentures (page:50). The Q2 10-Q gives a restricted versus unrestricted consolidating view of the balance sheet and statement of operations (page:50-51); the 10-K and earlier 10-Qs give the same view for their dates (10-K page:193-195; Q1 10-Q page:49; Q3 2025 10-Q page:66-67).

The notes and their individual issuers and guarantors beyond these passages are an unresolved distinction, not a conclusion. The pack gives the 2026 unsecured notes ranking language (10-K page:201) but no executed indenture, no guarantor schedule and no subsidiary exhibit text. The context names no borrower, parent or guarantor.
### Period basis and version relationships

The perimeter changes within the pack. Fiscal 2025 in the 10-K holds Old Uniti for seven months and the combined company for five (page:19, 10-K page:135). Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 are combined-company quarters whose comparative quarters are Old Uniti only (Q2 10-Q page:11). The Q2 10-Q states that the Windstream operations generated revenues and sales of 795.9 million and operating income of 69.7 million for the three months and 1,605.2 million and 173.0 million for the six months (page:19). It also gives unaudited pro forma comparatives, as if the merger had occurred on 2024-01-01, for the three and six months ended 2025-06-30 (page:19-20). The 10-K gives a pro forma table for the years 2025 and 2024 (page:135). Each pro forma table adjusts for the settlement of preexisting relationships, intangible amortization and other items and is stated to be for information only (page:20). A last-twelve-months figure on the combined perimeter is therefore not available directly from reported figures; it would need pro forma inputs with their labels, which is downstream work.

Statements of operations were reclassified in 2026: the prior-period Old Uniti statements were recast to show sales revenues apart from service revenues, to split cost of services from cost of sales, to add an operating income subtotal and to show loss on extinguishment of debt apart from interest expense, with no effect on net income (page:11). The prior-period cash flow statement was also reclassified (page:12). Comparative columns in the 2026 10-Qs are on this recast basis; the FY2025 10-K and the Q3 2025 10-Q are not.

Quarter versus year to date: the Q2 10-Q and release give three-month and six-month columns (page:5, release page:1). Q1 2026 stands alone in its own 10-Q and release, so each discrete 2026 quarter is available without subtraction. The fourth quarter of 2025 is in the release (page:1) and is derivable from the year and the 10-Q nine-month figures, which is downstream work, not done here.
### Debt, liquidity and subsequent-event evidence present

The Q2 10-Q debt note (page:20-22) lists, at 2026-06-30 and 2025-12-31, the Uniti and Windstream revolvers, the 2025 term loan, six senior note series, the 7.50% convertible senior notes due 2027 and six Fiber Infrastructure ABS series plus three Kinetic ABS 2026-1 series, each with principal, coupon, maturity and unamortized premium or discount. The Windstream term loan was repaid on 2026-02-04 (page:24). Liquidity is stated in the 10-Q (page:83): cash on hand, letters of credit and available revolver capacity. The two revolvers are described with their commitments, maturity date of 2027-12-30, letters of credit and amounts available (page:23-24). Covenants appear in general terms: the debt agreements require certain financial ratios and "the Company was in compliance with all of its debt covenants" (page:22). Pricing grids and mandatory prepayment step-downs refer to leverage ratios without printing the levels in force (page:23-25). The 10-Q prints interest paid and income taxes paid for six months only (page:13). Interest rate swaps and a terminated cap are described (page:32-34).

Subsequent events at the filing date, all inside the cutoff: the Kinetic ABS Series 2026-2 Notes issued on 2026-07-15 with classes A-2, B and C, the associated increase of the liquidity funding note facility, and a term loan prepayment offer and asset sale offers announced on 2026-07-23 with a partial repayment on 2026-07-30 (page:52-54, page:63). The release dated 2026-07-30 also updates 2026 outlook (page:2). The outlook is a management forward-looking statement, not a fact.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Uniti is highly leveraged and loss-making: total debt was 7.16x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at 2026-06-30, cash interest cover was 1.94x, and liquidity was 1,447.0 million. Heavy fiber capital spending is outspending operating cash flow. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is a company measure and trailing figures mix a smaller pre-merger company with the combined company. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt principal was 10,680.6 million at 2026-06-30, up from 9,540.5 million at 2025-12-31, as new asset-backed notes replaced revolver and term loan borrowings. | More debt is secured on subsidiary assets that sit outside the main credit group, which can matter for unsecured holders. | High |
| Operating cash flow was 339.4 million for the first half of 2026, against capital expenditures of 799.2 million. | The build-out is funded by debt issuance rather than internal cash flow. | High |

| Debt maturities are light in 2027 to 2028 and heavy from 2031, with 3,410.1 million due in 2031 and 2,595.0 million in 2032. | Near-term refinancing need is small; the later wall depends on market access. | Medium |

### Financial base view

The financial base is usable with limitations. Reported figures for Q1 2026, Q2 2026 and the first half of 2026 come from filed statements on the combined-company perimeter and tie to the releases. FY2025 holds the combined company only from 2025-08-01, so trailing and annual metrics are not like-for-like and are labelled that way. On the filed numbers, total debt principal of 10,680.6 million stood at 7.16x trailing-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 1,492.2 million, and 6.75x after deducting 608.9 million of unrestricted cash. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA covered trailing cash interest paid of 768.6 million 1.94 times. Interest expense, net was 383.9 million in the first half of 2026 against GAAP operating income of 143.1 million, so the company reports a net loss of 226.2 million for the half. Operating cash flow of 339.4 million fell short of capital expenditures of 799.2 million, and the gap was funded by debt: 2,072.6 million of issuance against 930.0 million of repayments. Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was cash of 608.9 million plus 838.1 million of revolver availability. Four limits bind every metric: Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure defined to resemble debt agreement terms but not tested here; the trailing period includes July 2025 without Windstream; covenant levels are not printed; and quarter-end debt does not include the July 2026 asset-backed issue or the planned repayments.
### Perimeter and period basis

- Reporting entity: Uniti Group Inc. and subsidiaries, consolidated. Old Uniti is the accounting acquirer, so periods before 2025-08-01 show Old Uniti only and later periods show the combined company (Q2 10-Q page:11, page:19).
- FY2025: audited, with PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP's opinion (10-K page:95-99). It contains seven months of Old Uniti and five months of the combined company.

- 2026 quarters: unaudited, combined company. Their comparatives are Old Uniti only and recast for the reclassifications described in the Q2 10-Q (page:11-12). Year-on-year changes are therefore not organic. The Q2 10-Q states that Windstream contributed 795.9 million of the quarter's 909.7 million revenue (page:63).

- FY2025 net income of 1,304.7 million includes a gain on settlement of preexisting relationships of 1,683.9 million (10-K page:101, page:88). The gain is excluded from Adjusted EBITDA. FY2025 reported EBITDA of 2,620.6 million (page:88) includes it and must not be used as a leverage denominator.

- Fiber Infrastructure revenue fell from 300.7 million in Q2 2025 to 200.3 million of external revenue in Q2 2026 because Windstream lease revenue ended on the merger; the filing attributes the decrease to the settlement of the preexisting leasing relationships (Q2 10-Q page:47, page:70).

### Income statement and operating drivers

- Revenue: Q2 2026 revenue was 909.7 million and Q1 2026 987.5 million. The Q1 figure includes the IRU sales revenue of 85.5 million for the first half; Q1 sales revenues were 98.5 million and Q2 56.8 million (Q1 10-Q page:4; Q2 10-Q page:4, page:63). Service revenues were 889.0 million in Q1 and 852.9 million in Q2, which is lower in Q2.

- Margins: Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 357.1 million was below Q1 2026 at 441.6 million, and the 2026 outlook issued 2026-07-30 is Adjusted EBITDA of 1,450 to 1,500 million, interest expense, net of 805 million and a net loss of 480 to 530 million (release page:2). That outlook is a management forward-looking statement. First-half Adjusted EBITDA of 798.7 million implies a second-half range of 651.3 to 701.3 million to reach it (calculated).

- Segments, Q2 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:47-49): Kinetic external revenue 528.2 and contribution margin 228.4; Fiber Infrastructure external revenue 200.3 and contribution margin 121.8; Uniti Solutions external revenue 181.2 and contribution margin 91.8; total segment contribution margin 442.0. Corporate and shared operating expenses were 86.7. Segment contribution margin is not Adjusted EBITDA.
- Kinetic fiber consumer broadband customers were 602.8 thousand and DSL customers 357.6 thousand at 2026-06-30 (page:70).
### Cash flow and funding

- H1 2026: operating cash flow 339.4; capital expenditures 799.2, of which Kinetic 602.8 (page:6, page:48). Operating cash flow less capital expenditures is negative 459.8 (calculated). Government grants were a separate offset: capital expenditures funded by grants 34.8 and grant funds received 11.9.

- Financing: debt issuance 2,072.6, repayments 930.0, financing costs 39.7 and preferred dividends paid 16.7, net financing inflow 1,077.8 (page:6). Cash plus restricted cash rose from 134.1 to 732.7.
- FY2025: operating cash flow 350.2 and capital expenditures 787.8, a negative 437.6 (calculated) (10-K page:102-103).
### Capital structure and debt detail

At 2026-06-30 (Q2 10-Q page:20-22): Uniti Revolver 500.0 commitment (undrawn); Windstream Revolver (undrawn); 2025 Term Loan 995.0; 4.75% secured notes 570.0 due 2028; 8.25% secured notes 2,200.0 due 2031; 7.50% secured notes 1,400.0 due 2033; 6.50% unsecured notes 1,110.0 due 2029; 6.00% unsecured notes 700.0 due 2030; 8.625% unsecured notes 1,600.0 due 2032; 7.50% convertible notes 306.5 due 2027; Fiber Infrastructure ABS notes 839.0 (six classes, 2030 and 2031); Kinetic ABS 2026-1 notes 960.1 due 2031. Principal totals 10,680.6; carrying value is 10,636.6 long-term plus 10.0 current after 34.0 of unamortized discount and costs.

- Change in H1 2026: the Windstream Term Loan of 500.0 was repaid in full on 2026-02-04 and 315.0 of Windstream Revolver borrowings repaid, using the proceeds of 1,000.0 of new 8.625% notes (principal rose from 600.0 to 1,600.0) and the 960.1 Kinetic ABS 2026-1 notes (page:21, page:24, page:26-27).

- Secured and structurally senior debt: the credit facilities and secured notes share first-priority collateral under an intercreditor agreement (page:25). The ABS notes are issued by bankruptcy-remote unrestricted subsidiaries (page:50), so their assets and cash flows sit outside the restricted group that supports the other debt. At 2026-06-30 unrestricted subsidiaries held total assets of 2,007.7 of 12,980.9 consolidated (page:50).

- Floating rate: only the 2025 Term Loan (995.0) and any revolver borrowings are variable; the Q2 10-Q reports a 7.65% weighted average rate on the term loan for the quarter (page:25) and four pay-fixed swaps: one of 200.0 assumed in the merger and three of 150.0 each (450.0) after a partial termination on 2026-01-28, 650.0 of notional in all against 995.0 of term loan (page:32, calculated sum).

| Letters of credit | 136.9 at 2026-06-30, of which 136.6 under the Windstream Revolver | No; reduce revolver availability | Q2 10-Q page:23-24, page:83 |
| Warrants | About 17.6 million warrants at 0.01 dollar exercise price issued to Windstream equityholders | No; equity | Q2 10-Q page:10 |
| Accrued interest | 148.4 at 2026-06-30 | No; working capital | Q2 10-Q page:5 |
### Liquidity and covenants

Liquidity at 2026-06-30 was 1,447.0, from cash of 608.9 and availability of 838.1 (calculated; page:83). Both revolvers mature 2027-12-30, 18 months after the balance sheet date, so neither is current yet; the Windstream Revolver commitment steps down to 425.0 after 2027-01-23 (page:24). Cash at quarter end excludes the July 2026 asset-backed proceeds: of the 1,140.7 raised, 500.0 is planned for repayment of secured debt and the balance for reinvestment (page:52).

Covenants: the debt agreements contain financial ratio covenants and the company reports compliance with all debt covenants at 2026-06-30 (page:22). Maintenance test names, levels, step-downs and reported ratios are Not supplied; the revolver margins and the term loan prepayment step-downs refer to leverage ratios whose levels are not printed (page:23-25). The company states that Adjusted EBITDA is calculated similarly to defined terms in its debt agreements (page:90-91). Headroom is therefore Not calculable.
### Subsequent events

All within the cutoff. Kinetic ABS Series 2026-2 notes of 1,140.7 (805.2 class A-2 at 5.834%, 134.2 class B at 6.224%, 201.3 class C at 7.536%) were issued on 2026-07-15 with anticipated repayment in June 2033; proceeds bought assets from subsidiary guarantors of the company's senior debt (Q2 10-Q page:52). A term loan prepayment offer of up to 167.8 on the 2025 Term Loan was issued 2026-07-23 and 19.8 was repaid on 2026-07-30; asset sale offers for up to 332.2 of the 4.75% and 7.50% secured notes opened 2026-07-23 (page:63; release page:2). The release gives an expiry of 2026-08-20 for the asset sale offers; their outcome is Not supplied. Pro forma for the prepayment of 19.8 and full use of 500.0, the figures above would change, but the amounts taken up are not supplied, so no pro forma leverage is computed.
### Definition and data-quality notes

- Adjusted EBITDA and EBITDA are company non-GAAP measures reconciled in each filing; the company excludes stock-based compensation, transaction related and other costs, the 1,683.9 gain and loss or gain on asset retirements (10-K page:88; Q2 10-Q page:91). They are not the covenant EBITDA of the executed agreements, which are not supplied.

- Quarterly cross-check: Q3 2025 Adjusted EBITDA 327.8 (Q3 2025 10-Q page:120) plus Q4 2025 365.6 (release page:1) plus Q1 2026 441.6 plus Q2 2026 357.1 equals 1,492.1, against 1,492.2 from the year-based method. The 0.1 difference is rounding in the printed figures.
- Releases match the filings: Q2 2026 net loss 155.9 and Adjusted EBITDA 357.1; Q1 2026 revenue 987.5 and Adjusted EBITDA 441.6. No conflict found.

- The FY2025 10-K also gives an unaudited pro forma table as if the merger occurred on 2024-01-01 (page:135). Pro forma Adjusted EBITDA is not printed in the sources read, so no pro forma leverage is computed.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Uniti is a fiber network operator formed by the 2025-08-01 merger of Old Uniti and Windstream, with Elliott holding about 25.2%. It is funding a large fiber build with debt, increasingly through asset-backed notes held in unrestricted subsidiaries. | Medium | No executed indentures or credit agreements are supplied, so creditor protections and basket capacity on asset transfers are not verified. |

### Business and transaction view

Uniti Group Inc. is a Delaware holding company that survived the 2025-08-01 merger of Windstream and Old Uniti as the ultimate parent. Old Uniti was a REIT that owned and leased communications infrastructure, with Windstream as its anchor tenant; after the merger it ceased to be a REIT and the company does not qualify as one. The combined business has three segments. Kinetic sells consumer and small business broadband and voice in incumbent markets. Fiber Infrastructure sells enterprise, carrier and wholesale connectivity, including to hyperscalers, and holds the legacy fiber and leasing assets. Uniti Solutions sells managed network, security and collaboration services to enterprises. The credit story is the build-out of fiber to the home at Kinetic and of wholesale fiber, funded by debt. The creditor-relevant mechanics are these. First, the perimeter changed, so history before the merger is Old Uniti. Second, all pre-merger debt of Old Uniti and Windstream was merged into one borrower, Uniti Services LLC, with cross-guarantees and the removal of restrictive covenants that kept the groups apart. Third, since 2026-01-30 the company has financed Kinetic through asset-backed notes issued by bankruptcy-remote unrestricted subsidiaries that hold the fiber assets and customer contracts, which places those assets and their cash flows ahead of other creditors for those noteholders. Fourth, Elliott and its affiliates hold about 25.2% of the common stock and have rights tied to the preferred stock. Fifth, the company states that it does not intend to pay common dividends. No sponsor is named in the context. Behaviour toward creditors is read as neutral or mixed on documented actions: refinancing that extended the maturity profile and transparent disclosure of unrestricted subsidiary results on one side, and transfers of assets from guarantor subsidiaries into unrestricted asset-backed structures on the other. Legal capacity for those transfers depends on indenture terms that are not supplied.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The Merger. On 2025-08-01 Windstream merged into the company, which survived as ultimate parent, and a merger subsidiary merged into Old Uniti, which survived as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary (Q2 10-Q page:9). Each Old Uniti share converted into 0.6029 shares of the company's common stock. Windstream's equityholders received about 90.1 million common shares, about 0.6 million preferred shares with a liquidation preference of 575.0, about 17.6 million warrants at a 0.01 dollar exercise price and 370.7 of cash, funded from Old Uniti's cash and revolver borrowings (page:10). The accounting is a reverse merger: Windstream was legal acquirer and Old Uniti was accounting acquirer (page:10). Total merger consideration was 2,376.6, made up of common stock 733.7, preferred stock 630.4, warrants 142.7, cash 370.7 and 499.1 attributed to the settlement of preexisting relationships (page:16). Those relationships were the Windstream Leases (an ILEC master lease and a CLEC master lease under which Old Uniti was Windstream's landlord), an asset purchase agreement and other leasing and supplier arrangements; they became intercompany and eliminated, and the leases were judged above market by 559.0 against an unfavourable asset purchase agreement of 60.0 (page:17-18). Status: complete; purchase price allocation finalised in Q2 2026 (page:18). Credit meaning: the Windstream lease payments that Old Uniti received as landlord ceased to be external revenue; creditors of the two former groups now rank in one structure.

Debt reorganisation. On 2025-08-04 Uniti Group LP, the borrower under Old Uniti's debt, was merged into Uniti Services LLC, formerly Windstream Services, LLC, the borrower under Windstream's debt. All debt became obligations of the same borrower, each subsidiary that guaranteed one group's debt guaranteed the other's, the Windstream revolver became pari passu with other first lien debt, and restrictive covenants that kept the groups apart were effectively eliminated (10-K page:56). Credit meaning: structural separation between the two creditor groups ended; the combined guarantor group supports all debt.
New debt issues, in date order, with status (all amounts in the financial base or the debt tables):

- October 2025: 1.4 billion of 7.50% senior secured notes due 2033 and a new seven-year 1.0 billion term loan due 2032; proceeds redeemed in full the 10.50% secured notes due 2028 and added more than 100.0 of liquidity; 250.0 of secured fiber network revenue term notes with anticipated repayment in January 2031 were also issued (10-K page:56). Status: complete.
- 2025: 600.0 of 8.625% senior unsecured notes issued 2025-06-24 under an indenture with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas as trustee (Q2 10-Q page:26). Status: complete.

- 2026-01-30: Kinetic ABS 2026-1 notes of 960.1, secured by fiber network assets and residential customer contracts in Texas, Arkansas, Kentucky, Ohio and Georgia that were sold to the ABS obligors, which are unrestricted subsidiaries; no recourse to the company or other subsidiaries (Q2 10-Q page:26-29). The notes pay interest monthly, have no scheduled principal before the anticipated repayment date in February 2031, and carry rapid amortization if a debt service coverage ratio is not maintained (page:28, page:30). The indenture also provides for a variable funding note facility and up to 14.0 of liquidity funding notes, none outstanding (page:28-29). Status: complete.

- 2026-02-04: 1.0 billion of 8.625% senior unsecured notes due 2032, expected to be exchanged for additional notes fungible with the existing 600.0; proceeds repaid the 500.0 Windstream Term Loan, revolver borrowings and funded general purposes including success-based capital expenditures (page:26). Gain on extinguishment of 1.2 (page:30). Status: complete.

- 2026-07-15 (subsequent event): Kinetic ABS 2026-2 notes of 1,140.7, anticipated repayment June 2033, bought assets held by subsidiary guarantors of the company's senior debt that were contributed to Kinetic ABS subsidiaries; the company intends 500.0 of net proceeds to repay senior secured debt through a term loan prepayment offer and asset sale offers, and the rest for reinvestment including growth capital spending (page:52). Status: complete for the notes; the repayment offers were open at the filing date and their uptake is not supplied.

- 2026-07-23 and 2026-07-30: term loan prepayment offer of up to 167.8, of which 19.8 was repaid on 2026-07-30, and asset sale offers for up to 332.2 of the 4.75% and 7.50% secured notes expiring 2026-08-20 unless extended (page:63; EX-99.1 2026-07-30 page:2). Status: outcome not supplied.

Credit meaning of the new issues: they extended the maturity profile and moved the funding of the Kinetic build to asset-level debt. The ABS structure ranks the noteholders first against the transferred assets, and the asset sale offers show that part of the proceeds is required to repay secured debt because the assets came from guarantor subsidiaries. How much cushion the restricted group retains depends on indenture terms that are not supplied.

### Reader summary

### Credit view

Uniti Group Inc. carries a weak fundamental credit profile with adequate near-term liquidity. The assessment is an Analyst Interpretation with Medium confidence. Financial risk dominates. At 2026-06-30 total debt principal of 10,680.6 million was 7.16x trailing Adjusted EBITDA and 6.75x net of unrestricted cash, and trailing Adjusted EBITDA covered trailing cash interest paid 1.94 times. Adjusted EBITDA is a company measure that excludes transaction costs and stock-based compensation, and the trailing window includes one pre-merger month. Cash generation does not support the investment programme: first-half 2026 operating cash flow of 339.4 million compared with capital expenditures of 799.2 million, so the build is financed with new debt, and the company reports a net loss in each of Q1 2026 and Q2 2026. Business risk is moderate. Uniti has three segments, no customer above 10% of revenue, a large fiber footprint, and a Kinetic fiber build that management intends to raise penetration and revenue per customer (management strategy), but the Fiber Infrastructure revenue base reset when Windstream's lease income ended on 2025-08-01, hyperscaler IRU revenue is lumpy, and the DSL base is declining. Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months: 1,447.0 million of cash and revolver availability at 2026-06-30, no instrument maturing before the 2027-12-01 convertible notes and the 2027-12-30 revolver maturities, and 1,140.7 million of further asset-backed proceeds in July 2026 of which 500.0 million is planned for secured debt repayment. Creditor control and structure add risk: the share of debt in non-recourse asset-backed subsidiaries is rising, and covenant levels and executed documents are not supplied. The credit view is therefore that earnings must grow into the debt through the fiber build while market access stays open; the filings contain no evidence that either is secured.
### Key findings

- Leverage and cover are weak, and the apparent improvement is partly a perimeter effect. Total debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 8.13x at FY2025, 7.75x at the trailing period to Q1 2026 and 7.16x at the trailing period to Q2 2026, but each earlier ratio uses a window with fewer Windstream months, so the improvement is partly a perimeter effect rather than a deleveraging. Cash interest cover was 1.78x, 2.34x and 1.94x on the same windows. Mechanism (Analyst Interpretation): higher-cost debt added in 2026 (8.625% unsecured notes and the asset-backed notes) is likely to raise cash interest faster than Adjusted EBITDA at the current build stage. Implication: leverage tolerance is low and a modest earnings shortfall would push trailing cash interest cover to about 1.55x (illustrative, calculated below).

- Free cash flow is structurally negative while the build runs. Operating cash flow less capital expenditures was negative 459.8 million in H1 2026 and negative 437.6 million in FY2025. Adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditures for the trailing period was 151.4 million (calculated below), which does not cover trailing cash interest paid of 768.6 million. Mechanism: capital expenditures at Kinetic of 602.8 million in H1 2026 front-load cost before subscriber revenue. Implication: the company depends on debt issuance or asset monetisation to fund both the build and interest, and creditors depend on continued access to the asset-backed and bond markets.

- Management's 2026 outlook implies interest absorbs most of the trend in earnings. The outlook for Adjusted EBITDA is 1,450 to 1,500 million, interest expense, net 805 million and a net loss of 480 to 530 million (management forward-looking statement). Against first-half interest expense, net of 383.9 million, the outlook implies about 421.1 million in the second half (calculated). Outlook Adjusted EBITDA covers outlook interest expense, net 1.80x to 1.86x (calculated). Implication: GAAP losses persist through 2026 on the company's own outlook.

- Maturity profile is back-ended by instrument due dates but the printed table conflicts. By due date, 876.5 million falls due in 2027 and 2028 (the convertible notes and the 4.75% secured notes) and 7,405.1 million in 2031 to 2033. Within that, the 6.50% unsecured notes of 1,110.0 million fall due in 2029, and the 8.625% unsecured notes plus the 2025 Term Loan, 2,595.0 million together, fall due in 2032. The Q2 10-Q prints a maturity table that places 886.5 million in 2027 and 1,120.0 million in 2028, which differs from the due dates by one year for 2027 to 2030; the Q1 10-Q table agreed with the due dates. This corrects the financial base handoff, which said no maturity table was printed: one is printed at Q2 10-Q page:30. The credit view uses the due dates and flags the conflict. Implication: the wall by year is uncertain by one year for 2027 to 2030 until the company confirms the schedule; the total is not in question.

- Structural priority is shifting toward asset-level debt. Of total principal, 6,964.1 million is secured (credit facility and secured notes 5,165.0 million plus asset-backed notes 1,799.1 million) and 3,716.5 million is senior unsecured, including the 2027 convertible notes (calculated; the convertible notes are described as senior unsecured at 10-K page:147). The asset-backed notes sit in unrestricted subsidiaries that hold fiber assets and customer contracts transferred from non-securitization subsidiaries, with no recourse to the company. After the July 2026 issue the asset-backed share rises from 16.8% to about 24.9% of principal before any repayments (calculated). Mechanism: assets move from the guarantor group to separate noteholders, so value available to the unsecured notes and the other secured creditors falls, and the asset sale offers show part of the proceeds must repay secured debt. Implication: unsecured holders are the most exposed to asset transfers. Legal capacity for transfers depends on indenture terms that are not supplied.

- Liquidity is adequate but supplied by financing, not operations. Cash of 608.9 million and revolver availability of 838.1 million give 1,447.0 million; the Uniti Revolver provides 499.7 million and the Windstream Revolver 338.4 million after 136.6 million of letters of credit. Both revolvers mature 2027-12-30 and the Windstream Revolver commitment steps down after 2027-01-23. Implication: the revolver renewal in 2027 is the first liquidity event that depends on market conditions.

- Equity-like claims sit ahead of common equity and can become cash claims. The preferred stock has a liquidation preference of 575.0 million and an 11% dividend, which is about 63.25 million a year at the face rate (calculated), and Elliott affiliates may require repurchase after the tenth anniversary. Mechanism: the repurchase may be settled in cash or stock. Implication: not a near-term cash issue, but it is a long-dated claim that competes with debt refinancing.

- Data limits restrict the view. Covenant levels and compliance ratios, executed indentures and credit agreements, pro forma Adjusted EBITDA, the outcome of the July 2026 repayment offers and any report after 2026-07-30 are not supplied. A conflict on whether the 1.0 billion 8.625% notes are secured is logged and unresolved; the debt tables describe them as unsecured.
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths:

- Scale and diversification of revenue. Three segments, no customer above 10% of revenue, and a network of about 240,000 fiber route miles (Documentary Fact, from the business handoff). Mechanism: reduces dependence on any one customer after the merger ended the dependence of Old Uniti on Windstream. Implication: lower single-customer default risk than before the merger.

- Adequate near-term liquidity and no scheduled maturity before December 2027. Cash and revolver availability of 1,447.0 million, and no instrument maturing in the next twelve months other than term loan amortization (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Implication: low near-term refinancing and liquidity risk.

- Demonstrated capital markets access. The company completed asset-backed notes in January and July 2026, 1.0 billion of unsecured notes in February 2026, and a secured refinancing in October 2025 that redeemed the 10.50% notes due 2028 (Documentary Fact). Implication: supports refinancing, though at high coupons.

- Segment margins. Contribution margins of about 52% at Fiber Infrastructure, 50% at Uniti Solutions and 42% at Kinetic in Q2 2026 are stated by management (Management Language), before corporate costs. Implication: scope for operating leverage if revenue grows, not yet visible in cash flow.
- No common dividends. The company states no intention to pay common dividends (Documentary Fact). Implication: cash is retained for the build and debt service.

- Fiber customer growth. Kinetic fiber consumer broadband customers were 602.8 thousand at 2026-06-30 and management states record quarterly fiber net adds (Documentary Fact for the customer count; Management Language for the record claim). Implication: supports future recurring revenue, if build costs per premise are controlled, which is not shown.
Weaknesses:

- High leverage and thin cover. Total debt 7.16x and net debt 6.75x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, cash interest cover 1.94x (Documentary Fact and calculation from the financial base). Implication: little tolerance for earnings shortfalls or rate increases on the floating-rate term loan.
- Negative free cash flow from the build. Operating cash flow of 339.4 million against capital expenditures of 799.2 million in H1 2026 (Documentary Fact). Implication: reliance on external funding.

- GAAP losses. Net loss of 226.2 million in H1 2026 with interest expense, net of 383.9 million exceeding operating income of 143.1 million (Documentary Fact). Implication: earnings do not yet cover the interest burden on a GAAP basis.

- Comparability and earnings quality. The perimeter changed on 2025-08-01, Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure, and Q1 2026 included IRU sales revenue of 85.5 million for the half that is not recurring service revenue (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on recurrence). Implication: run-rate earnings are harder to judge than reported trailing figures suggest.

- Back-end loaded maturity wall and the shifting structure. Heavy 2031 to 2033 maturities, rising asset-backed debt in unrestricted subsidiaries, and a preferred stock claim with an Elliott repurchase right (Documentary Fact). Implication: refinancing risk is deferred rather than removed, and unsecured holders are more exposed to asset transfers.

- Disclosure gaps and inconsistencies. No covenant levels, no executed documents, and two logged conflicts on ranking and the maturity table (Insufficient Information and Documentary Fact). Implication: the view cannot be tested against creditor protections.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Leverage and cover remain weak as capital spending exceeds cash flow | Debt-funded build adds interest before earnings arrive; floating-rate term loan adds rate exposure | Default risk rises if earnings growth or market access falters | Critical |

| Refinancing dependence on capital markets | Instruments mature mainly 2031 to 2033 and the revolvers mature 2027-12-30; the build requires continued issuance | Liquidity and refinancing risk if markets close | Material |

| Priming by asset-backed structures | Assets and cash flows are moved to unrestricted subsidiaries for non-recourse noteholders | Loss given default for other creditors rises; unsecured most exposed | Material |
| Earnings quality and comparability | Mixed perimeter, lumpy IRU sales revenue, company-defined Adjusted EBITDA | Leverage may be mis-measured; covenant EBITDA unknown | Material |

| Preferred stock and shareholder influence | 575.0 liquidation preference with repurchase right; 25.2% holder with board rights | Competing cash claim and governance influence over financing choices | Minor |
| Disclosure conflicts | Ranking of 8.625% notes and maturity table disagree within filings | Ranking and maturity timing uncertainty | Minor |

The cautious credit view with Medium confidence follows from the cited basis and is not overstated. ### Cross-module contradictions

One, resolved in favour of the later modules: CP-1 says no maturity table is printed, while CP-1A and CP-2 say one is printed and conflicts with the due dates. The Q2 10-Q page:30 confirms that a table is printed. Pairs examined and found consistent: leverage and cover in CP-1 against the weak profile in CP-2; adequate liquidity in CP-2 against negative free cash flow in CP-1; the rising asset-backed share in CP-2 against the transaction table in CP-1A; the no common dividend policy in CP-1A against the preferred dividends of 31.2 declared in H1 2026 in CP-1 (common equity versus preferred).
### Verdict consistency

The verdicts agree across modules for every shared claim except the maturity table statement. CP-2's confidence of Medium is no higher than the upstream limits allow, and its gap list contains the inherited gaps.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the cautious view is liquidity: cash of 608.9 and availability of 838.1 give 1,447.0 against no instrument maturity before 2027-12-01, and the company raised 1,140.7 more in July 2026. Segment contribution margins of about 52%, 50% and 42% suggest earnings power once the fiber build matures, and the 2026 outlook for Adjusted EBITDA of 1,450 to 1,500 compares with trailing 1,492.2, so the outlook range is close to the trailing figure. What would make that case win: capital expenditures falling after the build so that Adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditures covers interest, market access staying open for asset-backed and bond issuance, and the revolvers being extended before 2027-12-30. Downside chain with observable triggers: initiating condition, slower fiber penetration at Kinetic or fewer hyperscaler bookings; first operational break, Adjusted EBITDA below the low end of the outlook, which needs second-half Adjusted EBITDA of at least 651.3 (calculated); financial transmission, interest expense, net of 805 (outlook) then absorbs a larger share of earnings and cash interest cover falls below the trailing 1.94x; liquidity consequence, revolver drawings and letters of credit use the 838.1 of availability while capital expenditures continue; refinancing consequence, the 2027 maturities of the convertible notes and both revolvers meet a market that may be less open, while a failure of the debt service coverage test on the asset-backed notes would trigger rapid amortization of those notes (Q2 10-Q page:30). Observable triggers: quarterly Adjusted EBITDA against the 651.3 second-half requirement, the Windstream Revolver letter of credit balance, asset-backed debt service coverage disclosures, and the outcome of the asset sale offers.
